nodes.name: Liquid phase exfoliation and surface modification
nodes.procedure: Bulk BP crystals were initially ground with N-methyl pyrrolidone (NMP) for 30 min to create a coarse dispersion. This was followed by 10 h of bath sonication to produce the BP nanosheets (~300 nm in size). Subsequently, an excess of the predicted molecules was added. The mixture was stirred for 20 h in darkness under argon to obtain the modified BP samples.

nodes.description: Stability testing of BP microflakes on Si/SiO2 substrate via AFM
nodes.source_text: After exposure for 12 days, the atomic force microscopy (AFM) images of bare BP flake... show dense droplets... In contrast, the surfaces of P1 BPs MFs, S1-BPs MFs, and Si1-BPs MFs on the substrate are unchanged.

nodes.description: DFT simulation of water diffusion barrier through molecular passivation layers
nodes.source_text: the diffusion barrier (0.91 eV) for H2O approaching the BP surface is initially raised by the dense-packed molecular layers... The high energy barrier (1.30 eV) arises at the location of the -(SH)3 head group... S4 results in a higher diffusion barrier (1.01 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM images show dense droplets forming on bare BP and N-based modified BPs after 12-20 days, whereas P1, S1, and Si1 modified BPs remain unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: AFM images of bare BP flake ... show dense droplets and become larger at 20 days ... surfaces of P1 BPs MFs, S1-BPs MFs, and Si1-BPs MFs on the substrate are unchanged.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of Si1-BPs reveals a uniform ~3.7 nm organic layer and lattice fringes of 2.3 Å corresponding to the (014) plane of BP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-TEM images of Si1-BPs illustrate uniform ~3.7 nm organic layers ... lattice fringes of 2.3 Å corresponding to the (014) plane of BPs

nodes.characterization_summary: 1H NMR spectra confirm the presence of modified molecules (N2, P1, Si1, S1) anchored to the BP surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: 1H nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR) spectra for N2-BPs, P1 BPs, Si1-BPs, and S1-BPs show signals corresponding to the modified molecules ... effective anchoring

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR spectra show peaks at 1106, 1208, and 1126 cm-1 assigned to P-P-C, Si-O-P, and P-S bonds, indicating strong interfacial interactions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FTIR of P1 BPs, Si1-BPs, and S1-BPs reveal peaks at 1106, 1208, and 1126 cm-1, corresponding to P-P-C, Si-O-P, and P-S bonds respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Absorption spectra confirmed stability of P1, Si1, and S1 modified BPs for over 20 days in air compared to bare BP which degrades in 12 days.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This observation was also verified by the absorption spectra shown in Figure S7 ... the top-ranked new molecules P1-BPs, Si1-BPs, and S1-BPs exhibited markedly improved stability

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT calculations show molecule-BP interaction energies (Eint_BP) of -1.10 eV for P1, -1.02 eV for Si1, and -1.00 eV for S1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: DFT calculations show that their calculated molecule-BP interaction energies agree well with our GNN predictions ... P1 Eint_BP_DFT = -1.10 eV, Si1 Eint_BP_DFT = -1.02 eV, S1 Eint_BP_DFT = -1.00 eV
